To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
• Learner-centred, web-based assessment can be an effective way to build team skills in tertiary learners.

1) the online environment provides a unique opportunity to develop team skills; 2) team skills can be fostered by the use of online learning and assessment tools; 3) the online environment requires a different pedagogy to that of traditional classrooms; and 4) team skills are essential for the development of the graduate attributes required by the new economy.
a learner-centered approach to developing team and communication skills through web-based assessment is a useful and effective pedagogical tool.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a learner-centred approach through the use of web-based learning and integrated assessment.
the question: How can online assessment be used to support and foster team skills among learners?
the development and implementation of a model for the development of team skills through online collaborative learning.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the learner-centred approach is a successful way of developing team skills in online environments.
the learner-centred approach described here is a useful and effective means of developing the team skills of tertiary learners.

this approach has been successful in building the skills of collaboration among learners and in providing them with the opportunity to develop their skills of leadership, decision-making, conflict resolution and communication.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of web-based learning and integrated online assessments in a team learning environment can foster team skills.
the online team learning environment can be an effective tool for the acquisition and development of team skills, but that it needs to be designed and managed with care.

the use of online learning and assessment can be used to develop team skills and collaborative learning, provided that the design of the learning environment and the assessment tasks are carefully planned.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the development of teamwork and collaborative skills is not an automatic consequence of using online environments for learning.
online learning environments can be used as a platform to support team learning.
the online environment can support collaborative learning and assessment in ways that can be as effective as face-to-face learning.
